subject: Renewal: evidence ownership, rollforward plan & temporary seat/throughput ask
messages:
From: Olivia Barnes <olivia.barnes@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal checklist — question on retention and sequencing

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the kickoff yesterday. Procurement asked me to clarify two points before they start drafting the amendment: first, what retention window Redwood will commit to for audit logs as part of the renewal (13 months vs 24 months), and second, whether we can do a staged evidence upload (deliver high-priority artifacts first and follow up with lower-priority items).

We also have a short internal deadline: legal needs an itemized owner list for each artifact (who at Redwood will be the contact for infra/primary logs, and who will confirm sensitive-data redaction). Can you provide names?

I've attached our updated questionnaire (acme_questionnaire_v2.xlsx) — most of the items are routine but the log retention and seat/throughput uplift for the upload window are blockers.

Appreciate a quick reply — procurement is aiming for a signed amendment by mid-September.

Thanks,
Olivia Barnes
Security Program Manager
Acme Analytics

-----Original Attachment: acme_questionnaire_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia.barnes@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-30T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal checklist — question on retention and sequencing

Hi Olivia — thanks for sending the questionnaire and the clear ask. Quick answers up front: we can support a staged delivery for evidence, and we can commit to 13 months retention by default with a 24-month option (requires a small amendment and storage uplift). Below is a proposed bite-sized rollforward plan and ownership matrix so procurement/legal can see who to list on the amendment.

1) Prioritization (what we ship first)
   - Phase A (day 0–14): system architecture diagram, SOC 2 Type II last report, and index of audit logs with retention policy summary.
   - Phase B (day 15–45): extracted samples of audit logs (redacted), proof of KV cache controls, and user access review exports.
   - Phase C (day 46–90): full evidence bundle for selected controls, process docs, and any ops runbooks.

2) Ownership (Redwood contacts)
   - Logs & export process: Laura Bennett — Laura will own the S3 export location, manifest, and redaction guidance.
   - Infra & runtime evidence: Marcus Lin — Marcus will validate kernel/quantization runtime notes and provide the infrastructure diagram.
   - Program lead & contractual language: me (Karthik) — I'll coordinate timelines and the amendment language with procurement/legal.

3) Temporary capacity / seat uplift for evidence upload
   - Proposal: a short burst action — 2x throughput for up to 7 calendar days to speed bulk exports and uploads. If Acme prefers a longer window, we can extend to 14 days with a prorated charge.
   - We can offer a modest storage credit tied to the renewal if Acme signs the 24-month retention option.

4) Next steps / asks from Acme
   - Confirm retention preference: 13 or 24 months.
   - Confirm procurement timeline and whether procurement/legal want us to draft amendment language.
   - Indicate whether the burst throughput window is required and preferred duration.

Attaching an evidence_manifest_template.csv stub that Laura will use as the upload manifest. I'll follow up with concrete S3 paths and the export readme.

Karthik
Director, Compliance & Customer Security
Redwood Inference

-----Attachment: evidence_manifest_template.csv (CSV stub)
From: Olivia Barnes <olivia.barnes@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: 2026-08-31T08:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal checklist — question on retention and sequencing

Karthik — thanks, that plan is helpful and pragmatic. A few clarifications from our side:

- Retention: Acme will proceed with 13 months as the default for renewal. Procurement asked us to keep the 24-month option on the table for later discussion (they want pricing).

- Burst throughput: we will need the 2x throughput uplift for 10 days (we have a lot of historic logs to extract). Can Redwood confirm an upper-bound on daily export size and whether the burst can be scheduled during our weekend maintenance window?

- Amendment: Procurement would prefer Redwood draft the language for the retention and temporary throughput. If you can include the seat uplift (if any) and the storage-credit trigger, that will speed sign-off.

I can share a redline timeline from legal if that helps.

Thanks — Olivia

-----Inline: Acme notes — procurement target sign by 2026-09-15

Hi Olivia — looping in specifics from the infra side and answers to the burst questions. Forwarding my quick export plan below for your paperwork.

On Mon, 2026-08-30 at 11:05, Karthik Iyer wrote:
> (see prioritization and ownership matrix)

Export and retention notes (technical):
- Export surface: we will provide a pre-signed S3 location per evidence manifest row. Exports are compressed (gzip) and follow the prefix: s3://redwood-evidence/acme-ACME-4321/{control}/{date}/export.gz
- Daily export upper-bound we can support during the 2x burst: ~1.2TB/day sustained (this is conservative for planned uploads). If Acme needs more, we can schedule a short consultation with infra team — Marcus can lead.
- Redaction: we will provide a redaction script and guidelines; final redaction confirmation must come from Acme legal.

Billing / amendment notes:
- Temporary throughput (2x for N days): charged at a prorated throughput uplift rate. For renewals signed before 2026-09-15, we can offer a one-time storage credit up to $2,500 if Acme elects 24-month retention on top of the renewal.
- I'll prepare the S3 export readme (attached) and include the exact manifest fields. Karthik, I'll hand the amendment language back to you by EOD tomorrow so procurement has a starting draft.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Infrastructure PM, Redwood Inference
